findings.title: COVID-19 in wastewater
findings.headline: 100% of 2 samples positive, rising in Virginia
findings.meaning: A lot of COVID-19 in Virginia's wastewater, and it is rising.
findings.text: In Virginia during 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-26, data are partial with the latest sample on 2026-10-13. In the requested window, 2 samples from 2 sites were all positive (100.0%) with a mean concentration of 6,807.0 copies/g dry sludge. Compared with the preceding window 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-12 (23 samples, 60.9% positive, mean 30,912.5), the positive share rose by 39.1 percentage points while the mean concentration fell by 24,105.4. Earlier finding on record (mem_88d82b2fb7e4, 2026-10-27): SARS-CoV-2 detected in Virginia 2026-10-13..2026-10-26: 2/2 positive (100.0%), 2 sites, mean conc 6,807 (partial coverage, latest sample 2026-10-13); vs preceding window positive share rising (+39.1 pp).
facts: 100% of 2 samples were positive between 13 Oct and 26 Oct, from 2 sites
Latest sample 13 Oct (the data lags the end of the period)
Two weeks before: 61% positive, so the share is rising (+39 points)
caveats: No recent samples for Richmond City, so this is the state-wide reading, asked for again at the evaluator's request.
data lag: latest sample 2026-10-13 is before window end 2026-10-26

statements: SELECT MAX(sample_collect_date) AS latest_sample_date FROM wastewater.sars_cov_2 WHERE pcr_target = 'sars-cov-2'
SELECT MAX(sample_collect_date) AS latest_sample_date FROM wastewater.sars_cov_2 WHERE pcr_target = 'sars-cov-2' AND state_territory = 'va'

SELECT COUNT(*) AS samples, SUM(CASE WHEN pcr_target_detect = 'yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positives, COUNT(DISTINCT site) AS sites, AVG(CAST(REPLACE(pcr_target_avg_conc, ',', '') AS DOUBLE)) AS mean_conc FROM wastewater.sars_cov_2 WHERE pcr_target = 'sars-cov-2' AND sample_collect_date >= '2026-10-13' AND sample_collect_date <= '2026-10-26' AND state_territory = 'va'

SELECT pcr_target_units AS units, COUNT(*) AS samples FROM wastewater.sars_cov_2 WHERE pcr_target = 'sars-cov-2' AND sample_collect_date >= '2026-10-13' AND sample_collect_date <= '2026-10-26' AND state_territory = 'va' GROUP BY pcr_target_units ORDER BY samples DESC

findings.title: Flu (influenza A) in wastewater
findings.headline: 7% of 30 samples positive, rising in Virginia
findings.meaning: flu is showing up in a fair share of samples in Virginia, and the trend is rising.
findings.text: In Virginia during 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-26, data are partial with the latest sample on 2026-10-20. The window had 30 samples from 22 sites, with 2 positives (6.7% positive share) and a mean concentration of 1,907.7 copies/l wastewater (mixed units, indicative only). Compared with the preceding window 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-12 (81 samples, 0.0% positive, mean 1,682.4), the positive share rose by 6.7 percentage points and the mean concentration increased by 225.2. Earlier finding on record (mem_615ca91b46ed, 2026-10-27): influenza A detected in Virginia 2026-10-13..2026-10-26: 2/30 positive (6.7%), 22 sites, mean conc 1,908 (partial coverage, latest sample 2026-10-20); vs preceding window positive share rising (+6.7 pp).

Latest sample 20 Oct (the data lags the end of the period)
Two weeks before: 0% positive, so the share is rising (+7 points)
caveats: No recent samples for Richmond City, so this is the state-wide reading, asked for again at the evaluator's request.

findings.title: CDC guidance
findings.headline: CDC advice for visiting older adult
findings.meaning: What CDC recommends when visiting an older adult (65+)
findings.text:
What CDC recommends when visiting an older adult (65+):
- People 65 and older face higher risk of serious flu complications (about 70-85% of flu deaths in recent seasons). CDC prefers high-dose, recombinant or adjuvanted flu vaccines for this age group, ideally by the end of October. Anyone 65+ who develops flu symptoms should contact a healthcare provider promptly, as antiviral treatment is recommended for higher-risk people. [1]
- CDC recommends the 2025-2026 COVID-19 vaccine for people 6 months and older through individual-based decision-making, and says vaccination is especially important for people 65 and older, nursing-home residents and people at high risk of severe COVID-19. [2] (CDC's advice on this may have changed recently; check with a healthcare provider about what applies.)
- CDC recommends one RSV vaccine dose for everyone 75 and older, and for adults 50-74 at increased risk (e.g. chronic heart or lung disease, weakened immune system, living in a nursing home). It is a single dose, not yearly; late summer to early fall (August-October) is the best time. [3]
- If you have respiratory symptoms (fever, cough, runny nose), stay home and away from others. Resume normal activities only after at least 24 hours of improving symptoms with no fever (without fever-reducing medicine), then take extra care for 5 days: cleaner air, hand hygiene, a well-fitted mask, distance and testing, especially around people at higher risk. [4]
- CDC's core prevention steps are staying up to date on vaccines, washing hands, and cleaner air where people gather. Masks, distance and testing add protection when illness is rising in the community or when you are with someone at higher risk. [5]
This summarises CDC guidance (pages retrieved 2026-10-26); it is not personal medical advice.
caveats: COV-01: CHECK: refers to the 2025-2026 vaccine; look for a 2026-2027 update before the demo.
